compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
Intake deduplication is keyed on a ticket content digest that the platform's own write-backs mutate, so a ticket that has already been worked becomes re-admittable and starts a duplicate run.

The intake ledger records a SideEffectRef with operation intake_start and target built from the content digest and the repository. The platform writes back to the ticket during a run, adding comments and status changes, which changes the ticket content and therefore the digest. A later poll computes a different target, finds no matching ledger entry, and admits the ticket again. The active execution guard is the only thing preventing the duplicate, so the moment an execution row reaches a terminal state the ticket is eligible to run again.

Observed when intake admitted a duplicate run for ticket 53ed-ac2d-7739-4194 after its first run had already produced a pull request. The duplicate was intake-8383b6ac and was terminated manually at PLANNING.

The fix should key deduplication on ticket identity rather than on mutable content, while still allowing a deliberate re-run when an operator asks for one. Investigate how a re-run is meant to be requested before choosing the key, since the watermark poller currently relies on content changing to surface a ticket at all.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Intake deduplication is keyed on a value that the platform's own write-backs do not change
- [ ] A ticket that has already produced a run is not admitted again by an unrelated content change
- [ ] A deliberate operator requested re-run is still admitted
- [ ] The watermark poller still surfaces a ticket that has never been run

## Testing
Add unit tests under tests/unit covering the deduplication key and the re-run path, then run `pytest tests/unit -q` and `ruff check .`.
compiled_state.title: Key intake deduplication on ticket identity rather than mutable content
